cards.prompt: AI isn't only in chat apps. Remember: AI learns patterns from examples and makes guesses. Which of these use AI, and which just follow fixed steps someone wrote?

items.label: A photo app finding pictures of your dog
A map predicting traffic on your way
Live captions on a video as people talk
Your keyboard suggesting the next word
A calculator adding up a bill

cards.hint: Does the app have to make a guess from patterns it learned, or does it follow the same exact steps every time?
cards.nudge: Ask whether the app could ever be unsure. A guess from patterns can be wrong; fixed steps give the same result every time.
cards.explanation: Finding your dog, predicting traffic, writing captions and suggesting words are all **guesses** from learned patterns: AI. A calculator and an alarm follow **fixed steps**. Many AI features are switched on by default, and many can be turned off in settings.

cards.prompt: Some kinds of AI tool: a **chat assistant** writes replies to your messages, an **image generator** makes a picture from a description, a **voice assistant** answers out loud when you speak, and a **translation app** turns text into another language. Which would you use for each job?

pairs.left: Ideas for a birthday party, typed out
A picture of a dragon for a poster
A timer while your hands are covered in flour
A menu written in a language you can't read

cards.hint: For each job, what do you give the tool (typing, a description, your voice, some text), and what do you need back?
cards.nudge: Floury hands can't type, and a menu you can't read needs its words changed into your language.
cards.explanation: Typed questions suit a **chat assistant**, pictures come from an **image generator**, a **voice assistant** works hands-free, and a **translation app** changes the **language**. Many apps now do several of these.

cards.prompt: Some widely used AI chat assistants (A to Z) are **ChatGPT** (made by OpenAI), **Claude** (Anthropic), **Copilot** (Microsoft) and **Gemini** (Google). Many can also read files, search the web or make pictures. Your friend says: "My AI app is the best one. It's never wrong."

choices.text: "If it's the best, you don't need to check it"
choices.consequence: Even a very good model writes likely words, not checked facts. Every one of them can be wrong.

choices.text: "Every AI chatbot can be wrong, so check the things that matter"
choices.consequence: Right: they're all language models, so they can all hallucinate, whichever one is best at the moment.

choices.text: "Use the newest version: new ones don't make mistakes"
choices.consequence: Newer models can be better, but they still pick likely words, so they still make mistakes.

cards.hint: Think about how every chat assistant writes its answers, whichever company made it.
cards.explanation: Whatever the app, a chat assistant is a language model picking likely words, so **any** of them can be wrong. Check the things that matter.

cards.title: Age rules and good habits
cards.body:
Every AI app has its own rules, including **who can use it**. Some say 18 or older; some allow 13 with a parent's OK. Rules can differ by country, and they change.

- **Check the app's own rules**, and **ask a parent or carer** before signing up.
- **Think twice before uploading photos** of yourself or friends.
- **Follow your school's AI rules.**

cards.prompt: A new AI app promises to turn your selfie into a cartoon.

steps.text: It asks you to upload a selfie and a photo of a friend, and to tick "I am 18 or older". You're 13. What do you do?

choices.text: Upload only your own selfie, and leave your friend out
choices.consequence: Leaving your friend out is good, but the app still says 18 or older, and you're 13. It isn't for you yet.

choices.text: Stop, and ask a parent or carer about it
choices.consequence: Good: the app says it's for adults, and photos of you and a friend are worth a second thought.

choices.text: Ask your friend first, then upload both photos
choices.consequence: Asking your friend is a good habit, but the app is still for adults only. Ticking "18 or older" at 13 breaks its rules.

cards.hint: Look back at the age rules and good habits.
cards.explanation: The app's rules say 18+, so it isn't for you yet, even with only your own photo or your friend's OK. **Stop and ask a parent or carer.**

cards.prompt: For schoolwork, is each use of an AI tool **usually fine**, or one to **check with your teacher first**?

items.label: Explaining a topic you're stuck on
Spotting spelling mistakes in your notes
Making a picture for an art task

cards.hint: Does the AI help you learn, or does it make part of what you hand in?
cards.nudge: Does the AI make something that ends up in what you hand in?
cards.explanation: Help that lets you **learn** (explaining, quizzing, spotting spelling mistakes) is usually fine. Anything where AI **makes part of what you hand in** (writing, art, translation for a language task) is one to check with your teacher first.

cards.prompt: Is each one true of **every** AI chat assistant, or only **some** of them (or none)?

items.label: Writes its reply one word at a time

cards.hint: What do all of them share because of how they're built? What are extra features some apps add?
cards.nudge: Look for the ones that come from being a language model, and the ones that are extra features (or impossible).
cards.explanation: Every chat assistant is a language model: it **learned from text**, writes **a word at a time**, and **can be wrong**. Searching the web, making pictures and knowing today's news are **extra features** only some have, and none is never wrong.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Every chat assistant writes likely words, so any can be wrong.
- AI is also inside everyday apps: maps, photos, keyboards.
- Check each app's age rules, and ask a parent or carer.

Next: the module quiz.
